user_saw: Under a 768 MiB service memory limit, the Gateway was killed before it could deliver its first agent reply.
summary: The patch reduces Gateway startup memory pressure by deferring optional imports and warmups, retiring idle workers earlier, and shrinking emitted JavaScript.
reasoning: Path history shows that #120809 added eager reply-runtime prewarming to improve first-turn latency, and later commits had already reduced startup memory pressure. The available evidence establishes neither a working baseline at the 768 MiB cap nor a specific change that caused the Gateway to exceed it. The PR reports that the same out-of-memory failure persisted after this patch.
